title: Nine Weeks in Plaster
subtitle: 手臂与肢体 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 手臂与臂状物（人与自我·身体与健康）
meta: 主题语境：手臂与臂状物（人与自我·身体与健康）　|　核心词汇：arm　|　正文 322 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 arm 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my grandmother broke ① her arm reaching for a jar and said the jar was not worth it, and she was right. The ② arm, meaning the whole thing from the shoulder and not just the break, was in plaster for nine weeks; an arm, she said, is the only part of you that everybody else has to use. She said the jar was empty, which made it worse.

Every ③ arm in that house had a job, and hers was the jar shelf, which is the highest. Their ④ arm — the one the doctor wrote about — healed crooked, and she said a crooked arm is a straight arm that has decided something; an arm, my father said, is the only limb that apologises. He said hers never did.

My grandfather kept ⑤ arms, meaning the guns, in a cupboard he locked and never spoke about. The ⑥ arm, meaning the part of a body and not the weapon, is nine parts bone and one part habit, my grandmother said; an arm, she said, is the only thing in a house that can be both a tool and a threat. She said the cupboard was locked for eleven years.

The ⑦ arm of the river, where they fished in 1961, was nine yards wide and moved every year. By 1972 the ⑧ arm of her chair had worn through to the wood, and she said that was the honest arm; an arm, my father said, is any part of a thing that reaches out and holds nothing. He said a river does the same.

The ⑨ arm I remember is the one in plaster, which she used to point at things she wanted. An ⑩ arm, she said in 1981, is the only part of the body that can be given away and still be yours; every arm, she said, is either holding on or letting go. She said there is no third thing an arm can do.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 手臂（指整条手臂，与骨折处相对）
C. n. （复数 arms）武器；枪支
D. n. 手臂（指受伤后长好的那一条）
E. n. 臂状物（河湾、支流）
F. n. 扶手；臂状物（椅子的）
G. n. 手臂（抽象总称；泛指）
H. n. 手臂（一家人的、各自干活的）

items.q: The arm, meaning the whole thing from the shoulder
The arm, meaning the part of a body and not the weapon

answers.why: arm 意为“手臂、胳膊”，1959 年祖母伸手够一只罐子时摔断了胳膊，说那只罐子不值得。
arm 指“整条手臂”，与骨折处相对，从肩膀往下整条胳膊打了九个星期的石膏。
arm 指一家人的手臂（各自干活的），那屋里每一条胳膊都有活干，她的活是够最高的那一层罐子架。
arm 指受伤后长好的那一条，医生写的那条胳膊长歪了，她说歪胳膊是一条已经拿定主意的正胳膊。
arms 为复数，意为“武器、枪支”，祖父把枪锁在一个他从不出声提起的柜子里。
arm 意为“手臂（身体的一部分）”，与武器相对，是九分骨头加一分习惯。
arm 意为“臂状物、河湾、支流”，1961 年他们钓鱼的那条河湾宽九码，每年都在移动。
arm 意为“扶手、臂状物”，到 1972 年她那把椅子的扶手已经磨到木头，她说那是最诚实的胳膊。
arm 意为“手臂”，我记得的是打着石膏的那一条，她用这条胳膊指着她想要的东西。
arm 为抽象总称，泛指“手臂这种肢体”，她说手臂是身体上唯一能送出去却仍然是你的部分。
